correctness.rationale: Three-anchor extension is expressible with four variables. Conversely, when one of four pebbles is moved, at most three distinct anchors remain: reuse the corresponding vertex on an equality move and otherwise apply the extension axiom, padding to three anchors if necessary. This works at every finite quantifier rank in pure adjacency with equality. A mixed row–column–symbol triangle can have its required common neighbor only at the fourth corner of the corresponding rectangle, forcing equality of opposite entries. After symbol normalization, the relative row permutations are involutions; the row permutations then commute and act as a transitive, faithful abelian permutation group, hence regularly. This yields a Boolean-group table up to isotopy. Orders 2 and 4 lack an extension; in dimension at least 4, use anchors (0,0,0), (a,b,a+b), (c,d,c+d) with a,b,c,d independent. Any common neighbor would assign row, column and symbol bijectively to those anchors, producing a nontrivial linear dependence. For the remaining order 8, a fresh direct-coordinate exhaustion generated (r,c,r XOR c) for 0≤r,c<8, then for each unordered anchor triple counted all masks of adjacency attained by each of the 61 other vertices. All 333312 triple-pattern counts were positive, with minimum 1. The stated critical triple has the unique common neighbor (2,2,0), and coordinate translations carry that witness to every vertex. Thus deleting any vertex destroys 3-e.c.
residual_risks: The finite sufficiency computation is exhaustive only for the explicitly constructed 64-vertex graph; necessity for other sizes is the separate symbolic argument.
The conclusion is for at most four reusable variables at arbitrary quantifier rank, without counting or coordinate predicates.

value.rationale: The finite-logic question singles out one natural cell graph in an infinite class, not a graph selected for a one-off computation. The extension axiom forces isotopy to an elementary abelian group through a concrete local obstruction; the remaining finite case and its unique-witness deletion obstruction give sharp classification and minimality information.
residual_risks: The classification does not extend here to more parallel classes, counting logic, or arbitrary strongly regular graphs.
